detectiveClues.clueText: When Xavier died in a windswept reed hut on this island on December 3, 1552, four men packed his coffin with unslaked lime so they could later carry his bones to Goa—yet in February 1553 his body was still completely fresh!

detectiveClues.clueText: A scenic vineyard hill town in northern Croatia near the Slovenian border honoring ancient Stridon.

detectiveClues.headline: Historical Footprint
detectiveClues.clueText: Legend laughs that whenever Pope Sixtus V gazed at a painting of fiery St. Jerome beating his chest with a stone in repentance, the Pope remarked: "You do well to carry that stone, Jerome—without it, the Church would never have canonized you!"

detectiveClues.headline: Born on the Adriatic Frontier
detectiveClues.clueText: Born Eusebius Sophronius Hieronymus to a prosperous Christian family on the border of Dalmatia and Pannonia, brilliant young Jerome had an insatiable hunger for books—and a notoriously hot temper he wrestled with his whole life!

stops.title: Scholar on Rome’s Aventine Hill
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Aventine Hill to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.imageCaption: Scholar’s candlelit Roman study on the Aventine Hill with parchment Hebrew and Greek scrolls at dusk.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: On Sundays as a student in Rome, Jerome loved descending into the dark Catacombs to pray beside the tombs of the Apostles and early martyrs.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: Jerome’s monumental Latin Bible—the Vulgate ("common tongue")—became the standard Bible of Western civilization for over 1,500 years!
stops.saintQuote: Read the divine Scriptures constantly; never, indeed, let the sacred volume be out of your hand.

stops.imageCaption: Colossal sunlit imperial red-brick Aula Palatina basilica and misty Moselle meadows of 4th-century Trier.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: The colossal red-brick Aula Palatina (Basilica of Constantine) still towers over Trier exactly as young Jerome saw it in the 360s.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: Jerome’s own library of hand-copied Greek and Latin scrolls traveled everywhere with him in heavy leather trunks across three continents!

stops.title: Hermit & Lion in the Syrian Desert
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Desert of Chalcis to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.imageCaption: Solitary sandstone hermit cave overlooking golden limestone steppes of the Syrian desert with a gentle resting lion.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Artworks around the world still depict St. Jerome beside a loyal desert lion—from the famous medieval tale of a wounded lion limping into his monastery and letting Jerome pull a thorn from its paw.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: Jerome joked that learning harsh Hebrew pronunciation after smooth classical Latin nearly broke his teeth—yet it made his Vulgate Bible a masterpiece of scholarship.
stops.saintQuote: Good, better, best. Never let it rest. ’Til your good is better and your better is best.

stops.title: Thirty-Four Years in the Cave of Bethlehem
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across Bethlehem Study Cave to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.imageCaption: Candlelit limestone Study Cave of St. Jerome directly beneath the Basilica of the Nativity with open Hebrew and Latin scrolls.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Descending from St. Catherine’s Church beside the Basilica of the Nativity, pilgrims step straight into St. Jerome’s quiet rock-hewn Study Cave and tomb chapel.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: When Rome was sacked by barbarians in 410 AD and refugees flooded Bethlehem, aged Jerome dropped his pen immediately to house, feed, and comfort frightened families—proving Scripture always leads straight to love of neighbor!
stops.saintQuote: We must translate the words of Scripture into deeds.
